stem: A California prescriber issued an otherwise valid methylphenidate prescription six days ago. The patient presents it today at a Massachusetts pharmacy. Which threshold issue is dispositive?

choices.text: California is outside the narcotic contiguous-state list.
Methylphenidate becomes Schedule VI when issued outside Massachusetts.
The prescription is eligible because nonnarcotic Schedule II prescriptions have no timing gate.
The Massachusetts five-day presentation window has passed.

explanation.core_reasoning: Methylphenidate is a nonnarcotic Schedule II drug, so the narcotic issuing-state list is not the controlling branch. The prescription nevertheless fails the Massachusetts five-day presentation window on day six.

choice_analysis.A: The specified-state rule for out-of-state narcotic Schedule II prescriptions is not the controlling branch for methylphenidate.
choice_analysis.B: Issuing location does not change methylphenidate's controlled-substance schedule.
choice_analysis.C: The nonnarcotic pathway still has a five-day Massachusetts presentation window.
choice_analysis.D: This is correct because day six is outside the applicable threshold window.

related_facts: Passing an out-of-state threshold gate does not compel dispensing.
Authenticity and prescriber authority remain separate checks.
explanation.mpje_trap: Correctly identifying the nonnarcotic pathway but deleting its timing requirement.

reasoning_steps: Classify methylphenidate as nonnarcotic Schedule II
Apply the out-of-state five-day presentation window
